Seminar Title:

A Strata Mechanics Study for the Design of Fenders and Safe Cut-Out Distance under Different Geo-Mining Conditions during Mechanised Depillaring

Seminar Type:

Registration Seminar

Department:

Mining Engineering

Speaker Name:

Tamilprasanth M ( Rollno : 525mn6002)

Speaker Type:

Venue:

Seminar Room, Department of Mining Engineering

Date and Time:

20 May 2026 10:00 AM

Contact:

Sahendra Ram

Abstract:

Mechanised depillaring (MD) creates wider excavations, which are associated with significant strata movement. During MD, the geometry of the pillar continuously changes due to systematic extraction along a predefined line of extraction. Depending on the pillar dimensions, two different extraction approaches are generally adopted in continuous miner-based MD operations, namely split and non-split methods. The split method is commonly adopted for large pillars, where the pillar is divided into two or more parts for efficient slicing operation. The resulting fenders are slender (width-to-height ratio&lt5) in nature. Since these fenders are located adjacent to the active goaf, they are subjected not only to development load but also to additional abutment loads generated from the hanging roof inside the goaf. Under such conditions, estimation of fender load using the conventional tributary area method becomes inadequate. The competency of the overlying strata plays a critical role in governing roof caving behaviour and the associated load transfer mechanism. Several instability issues, including fender/pillar spalling, coal bumping, and deterioration in the performance of artificial support systems, are frequently observed in and around a pillar under extraction during MD operations. These issues lead to unsafe mining with reduction in recovery of coal. The safe cut-out distance (COD) is also significantly influenced by the abutment loads and competency of pillars within the active mining zone (AMZ). Therefore, an appropriate fender design methodology is essential to ensure safe and efficient extraction. In view of these challenges, this study aims to develop a suitable framework for safe fender design under varying overlying strata conditions. In addition, a coal bump potential assessment methodology specifically for Indian geo-mining conditions will be proposed, along with suitable coal bump mitigation strategies for MD with caving. A design framework for estimating safe COD during mechanised depillaring will also be developed. Overall, this study will address one of the major dynamic loading and stability challenges encountered during mechanised depillaring through detailed field investigations, laboratory, and numerical modelling analyses.
